summary: This work develops a microscopic noise model for multiqubit gates in trapped-ion systems by deriving effective single- and two-qubit error channels from phonon heating, motional dephasing, and photon scattering. The analysis shows that scattering errors and two-qubit errors from dephasing are largely confined to gate-coupled qubits, and demonstrates a finite threshold for surface-code error correction with physically realistic error rates.
motivation: Multiqubit gates enable all-to-all connectivity and reduced circuit depth in trapped-ion quantum computers, but their compatibility with quantum error correction hinges on understanding how noise propagates through the simultaneous multiqubit interactions, which differs substantially from the well-characterized two-qubit gate case.
method: The authors construct a detailed microscopic model by analyzing the Lindblad master equation in the rotated frame with respect to ideal gate evolution, then tracing out phonon degrees of freedom to extract effective Pauli error channels. They characterize three noise sources: photon scattering (via Raman transitions), phonon heating, and motional dephasing, deriving analytic leading-order expressions for error probabilities as functions of the phase-space trajectories $\alpha_j^{(n)}(t)$ and entangling phases $\phi_{nm}(t)$.
result: For a 37-qubit $d=5$ rotated surface code with stabilizer measurements via single multiqubit gates, the authors observe a crossing point at $p_c \approx 2 \times 10^{-2}$ when two-qubit errors between uncoupled qubits are included, and a clear threshold at $p_{\mathrm{th}} \approx 1.3\%$ when restricting two-qubit errors to gate-coupled pairs, demonstrating scalable quantum error correction with experimentally relevant parameters ($\Gamma_s \tau \approx 2.6 \times 10^{-4}$, $\Gamma_h n_{\mathrm{th}} = 50$ Hz, $\Gamma_d = 10$ Hz).
